title: Introduce invocation cooldown sampler and token-hash cost dashboard
author: Sofia Chen
description:
Motivation: Long-tail alert churn driven by bursty fanout patterns has been skewing token-cost alerts and obscuring real regressions. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: 1) an invocation cooldown sampler that reduces noise from rapid-fire fanout spikes by probabilistically suppressing redundant invocations within a short cooldown window while preserving representative samples, and 2) a token-hash cost dashboard that groups token-level cost and latency by stable token-hash buckets to surface hot tokens and amortized cost patterns across routes.

What this PR does: Adds a lightweight cooldown-sampler service inside the observability pipeline (configurable cooldown window, backoff behavior, tenant-aware sampling weight). The sampler emits enriched sample metadata (cooldown_reason, sampling_seed, tokens_sampled_count) which are joined into existing traces and metrics. Introduces a Grafana dashboard (Token Hash Cost Explorer) and a compact scatter panel visualizing prefetch vs. fanout impact per-token-hash. Adds new metrics: obs.cooldown.samples{reason}, obs.cooldown.skipped_ratio, obs.tokenhash.cost_p50/p90/p99, obs.tokenhash.latency_p50/p95 and a tag for token_hash.

Key design decisions: - Use deterministic token-hash bucketing (FNV-1a 64-bit) so samples are stable across nodes and reruns. - Sampler operates in the observability ingestion tier (post-ingress) to avoid perturbing serving pipelines. - Sampling policy is tenant-aware with an override table for tenants with dedicated SLOs.

Checklist: - [x] implement sampler and config knobs - [x] instrument metrics and spans - [x] add Grafana dashboard JSON + panels - [x] e2e smoke test for sample propagation - [x] update docs (observability sampler playbook)

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for sampler behavior and deterministic hashing included. Integration smoke test runs in perf-canary cluster. Rollout plan: feature gated behind obs.cooldown.enabled feature flag (default off) — stage: canary (10% tenants) -> 50% -> global. We will monitor obs.cooldown.skipped_ratio and tokenhash.cost_p99 regression for the first 72 hours.

Related: Linear ENG-4321 (noise-reduction for token-cost alerts), PM-98 (dashboard request). Links: internal RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/r/obs-sampler-rfc, dashboard preview: grafana/internal/d/tdash/token-hash-explorer.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing alert thresholds — the sampler provides a de-noised signal to downstream alerters which will be tuned in a follow-up PR.
